appropriate: a closed rounded tile split in two, the left half's half-disc seated in the right half's socket: still, exact and enclosing (Sage with Caregiver), but 'nothing gets dropped' or 'both sides' takes a sentence to reach
distinctive: no hook, arrow, node or hexagon and the amber is free in the category, but the silhouette is a plain rounded-square app tile; the split-and-socket is a detail, not an ownable outline
simple: one rounded square, one vertical cut, one half-disc tab; drawable from memory in seconds
legible: the cut and the curve stay visible down to 24 px and the 16 px tile still shows the curve, though the gap is near a hairline; 'Orvane' reads cleanly in every lockup
adaptable: black, reversed white-on-black, one colour at 64 and 32 px, the amber phone tile, browser tab, avatar and dark header all hold; the thin cut is the weak point at the smallest sizes
timeless: square, tile-aware geometry and a plain sans wordmark, no 'avoid' trend; nothing here would have dated ten years ago
universal: the mirrored panel reads clean, but rotated 90 the tile reads as a tray or a smiling face with the half-disc as a mouth
clear: unsearched: split rounded tiles with a socket-and-tab join are common in generic app icons and puzzle-piece marks; nothing I know in webhook tools (Svix, Hookdeck, Convoy, Hook0, ngrok) is close
congruent: warm amber against the blue category, softened corners on exact geometry, still and grounded, medium-heavy solid weight and a neo-grotesque title-case wordmark all match; the mark is left-right asymmetric against a 0.8 symmetry target and the wordmark is the category's Inter-like type
system: horizontal lockups on light and dark and a tier ladder from 256 to 16 px are shown, but no stacked lockup appears and the 16 px tier looks scaled rather than redrawn
